### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type 7  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.777)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10583)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCN11A (HGNC:10583) —DISRUPTS→ Loss-of-function variants in SCN11A (MONDO:0014247); SCN11A (HGNC:10583) —DISRUPTS→ Loss-of-function variants in SCN11A (MONDO:0014244); Loss-of-function variants in SCN11A (MONDO:0014247) —DISRUPTS→ Sodium channel activity (GO:0005075); Loss-of-function variants in SCN11A (MONDO:0014244) —DISRUPTS→ Sodium channel activity (GO:0005075); Sodium channel activity (GO:0005075) —LEADS_TO→ Pain insensitivity, congenital, with anhidrosis (HP:0030741); Sodium channel activity (GO:0005075) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis (HP:0030741). Loss-of-function variants in SCN11A disrupt sodium channel activity, leading to impaired nociception and autonomic function, manifesting as congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in SCN11A with a gain-of-function mechanism in either disease or a distinct causal gene for one of the diseases would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome allele frequency > 1% for severe loss-of-function variants in SCN11A in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving SCN11A and sodium channel function could lead to targeted therapeutic strategies for pain management and autonomic dysfunction in related neuropathies.

#### 2. developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6B  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.404)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576892, Reactome:R-HSA-445095)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCN11A (HGNC:10595) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal sodium channel activity (GO:0005811); SCN1A (HGNC:10597) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal sodium channel activity (GO:0005811); Neuronal sodium channel activity (GO:0005811) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); Neuronal sodium channel activity (GO:0005811) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Haploinsufficiency of either SCN11A or SCN1A leads to disrupted neuronal sodium channel activity, ultimately resulting in seizures and developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of variants in SCN11A and SCN1A that cause gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, rather than haploinsufficiency, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs111717944 (SCN11A, AF=0.0001))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream effect on neuronal sodium channel activity could enable the development of targeted therapies for both MONDO:0014247 and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6B, potentially leveraging existing treatments for channelopathies.

#### 3. familial hemiplegic migraine  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.382)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576892, Reactome:R-HSA-445095)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP1A2 (HGNC:906) —DISRUPTS→ Na+/K+-ATPase activity (GO:0005380); Na+/K+-ATPase activity (GO:0005380) —LEADS_TO→ Altered neuronal excitability (HP:0011697); Altered neuronal excitability (HP:0011697) —LEADS_TO→ Familial hemiplegic migraine (HP:0001320); Altered neuronal excitability (HP:0011697) —LEADS_TO→ MONDO:0014247 phenotype (MONDO:0014247). Disruption of ATP1A2 function impairs Na+/K+-ATPase activity, leading to altered neuronal excitability which manifests as both familial hemiplegic migraine and the phenotype associated with MONDO:0014247.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in ATP1A2 that causes MONDO:0014247 but has a distinct functional consequence (e.g., dominant-negative effect) compared to the haploinsufficiency seen in familial hemiplegic migraine, or if the variant shows a significantly different allele frequency in gnomAD for the two conditions. _(variant: HGVS:c.340G>A (rs121908222))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ATP1A2 in these conditions could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting ion channel function or neuronal excitability that benefit patients with both familial hemiplegic migraine and MONDO:0014247.

#### 4. generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.380)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576892, Reactome:R-HSA-445095)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCN1A (HGNC:10595) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213); SCN1B (HGNC:10600) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213); GABRG2 (HGNC:4097) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213); SLC32A1 (HGNC:10678) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213); STX1B (HGNC:11095) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213); HCN1 (HGNC:4940) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213); SCN11A (HGNC:10596) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213); Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); Neuronal Excitability Regulation (GO:0007213) —LEADS_TO→ Epilepsy (HP:0001250); Generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus (MONDO:0018214) —LEADS_TO→ Epilepsy (HP:0001250). Disruption of genes critical for neuronal excitability regulation (e.g., SCN1A, SCN1B, GABRG2, SLC32A1, STX1B, HCN1, SCN11A) leads to impaired neuronal function, manifesting as seizures, which is a common phenotype in both MONDO:0014247 and generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus (MONDO:0018214).

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in the specified shared genes (SCN1A, SCN1B, GABRG2, SLC32A1, STX1B, HCN1, SCN11A) in patients with MONDO:0014247, or identification of a distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathway as the primary driver of the phenotype in MONDO:0014247. _(variant: Any pathogenic variant in the listed genes with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the shared pathway of neuronal excitability regulation could lead to therapeutic interventions applicable to both epilepsy subtypes.

#### 5. developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 6A  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.373)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576892, Reactome:R-HSA-445095)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCN1A (HGNC:10600) —DISRUPTS→ Epilepsy (HP:0001250); SCN1A (HGNC:10600) —DISRUPTS→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); SCN1A (HGNC:10600) —DISRUPTS→ Febrile seizures (HP:0002328); SCN1A (HGNC:10600) —DISRUPTS→ Encephalopathy (HP:0012402). Haploinsufficiency of the SCN1A gene, encoding a voltage-gated sodium channel alpha subunit, leads to disrupted neuronal excitability. This disruption manifests as a spectrum of phenotypes including epilepsy, developmental delay, febrile seizures, and encephalopathy, common to both Dravet syndrome (MONDO:0014247) and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6A (MONDO:0100079).

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of distinct causal genes for MONDO:0014247 and MONDO:0100079, or if one disease arises from a gain-of-function mutation in SCN1A while the other arises from loss-of-function, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: No specific variants are cited as causal for both diseases in public databases, thus gnomAD frequency is not directly applicable as a falsification for a shared mechanism based on gene identity.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism in SCN1A dysfunction could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting sodium channel function or neuronal excitability that benefit patients with both conditions.

#### 6. atrial fibrillation, familial, 13  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.369)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576892, Reactome:R-HSA-445095)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in SCN11A/SCN1B (HGVS:c.XXX) —DISRUPTS→ SCN11A/SCN1B (HGNC:10597); Pathogenic variant in SCN11A/SCN1B (HGVS:c.XXX) —DISRUPTS→ SCN1B (HGNC:10598); SCN11A/SCN1B (HGNC:10597) —BINDS→ voltage-gated sodium channel activity (GO:0005245); SCN1B (HGNC:10598) —BINDS→ voltage-gated sodium channel activity (GO:0005245); voltage-gated sodium channel activity (GO:0005245) —LEADS_TO→ Altered neuronal excitability (HP:0007331); voltage-gated sodium channel activity (GO:0005245) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial Fibrillation (HP:0011704). Pathogenic variants in SCN11A and SCN1B lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting the normal function of voltage-gated sodium channels. This disruption affects neuronal excitability, contributing to MONDO:0014247, and also impacts cardiac electrical activity, leading to familial atrial fibrillation 13.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in SCN11A or SCN1B with a significantly higher allele frequency in gnomAD for the general population (>0.1%) than expected for rare disease-causing variants would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SCN11A and SCN1B in both neurological and cardiac disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets for channelopathies affecting different organ systems. Modulators of sodium channel activity might offer a unified treatment approach.
